pr_title: [stm32] PM restore console after sleep mode
pr_body:
With this change, the clock configuration is restored when leaving the low power mode. 
Then the console of the nucleo_wb55 can operate after sleeping.

The UART executes the `uart_stm32_set_power_state` to have a clean configuration before entering the low power mode.
On wakeup, the clocks are re-configured thanks to the `stm32_clock_control_init` function called directly in the 
`pm_power_state_exit_post_ops` of each soc.
This method is more efficient than introducing a _clock_stm32_pm_control_ function in the clock driver. 

Fix #31284
Requires #32042

Signed-off-by: Francois Ramu francois.ramu@st.com

issue_context.title: [stm32] PM restore console after sleep mode
issue_context.body:
When testing the PowerManagement on stm32L4 or stm32WB55 through the tests/subsys/power/power_mgmt
the console is no more functional and prints spurious characters.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
To define a function in the uart_stm32.c driver (replace _device_pm_control_nop_)  
to flush the  console before going to sleep 
To restore the correct clock for the console after sleep mode



**Console: **
```

Running test suite power_management_test                                        
===================================================================             
START - test_power_idle                                                         
give way to idle thread                                                         
 PASS - test_power_idle                                                         
===================================================================             
START - test_power_state_trans                                                  
�������������������������������������������������������������������������������

```
comments:
When considering STOP 0/1/2 low power modes as DEVICE_PM_LOW_POWER_STATE  for the stm32l4xx soc:
1) before going to sleep mode, wait for  USART Rx and Tx empty
2) USART is clocked by the PLL. During STOP mode the all clocks are OFF except LSE and LSI. After STOP mode HSI16 or MSI are wakeup clock, so the USART needs one of them or system must restore the PLL
3) in the test application tests/subsys/power/power_mgmt, the dummy_driver is put in DEVICE_PM_SUSPEND_STATE
not in DEVICE_PM_LOW_POWER_STATE
4) LPUART is not available on this nucleo board

In the test application tests/subsys/power/power_mgmt, the dummy_driver is put in DEVICE_PM_SUSPEND_STATE (=3)
Going to sleep mode the dummy driver is still in DEVICE_PM_SUSPEND_STATE (=3) when the irq (lptim) occurs and cause the system to wakeUp. 
On wakeUp, the `pm_notify_power_state_exit()` is called in the `pm_system_resume()`, "from the ISR of the event that caused exit from kernel idling after PM operations" _before_ the  `pm_resume_devices()` function.
The `pm_notify_power_state_exit`, implemented in the main.c, is checking the `device_power_state` of the dummy driver.
At this moment the `device_power_state` of the dummy driver is still DEVICE_PM_SUSPEND_STATE.
--> zassert_equal(device_power_state, DEVICE_PM_ACTIVE_STATE, NULL); **fails**
After that, the `pm_resume_devices()`, especially for the dummy_driver is setting back the device_power_state from DEVICE_PM_SUSPEND_STATE to DEVICE_PM_ACTIVE_STATE.
add the CONFIG_PM_DEVICE definition from the CONFIG_PM  for the soc that supports the low power modes.
Note that the `tests/subsys/power/power_mgmt_soc`  might requires a stack size with  `CONFIG_IDLE_STACK_SIZE=640` in its prj.conf

review_comments: Commit title not in line with content
`uart_stm32_pm_control()` is now also part of this #ifdef. Could this cause problems when `CONFIG_PM_DEVICE` isn't selected?
In case the PM_DEVICE is not defined, the uart_stm32_pm_control does not exist but  DEVICE_DT_INST_DEFINE gets a null value for this entry (no error).
It may be part of an `} else if () {`, then just return for the rest. If any `ctrl_command` gets added, this code could still be valid but would fail due to this assertion.
simplification in  testing only new_state != DEVICE_PM_ACTIVE_STATE

This does not _exactly_ set the power state, which is confusing to future readers. I suggest moving the `data->pm_state = new_state` from below to here, or rename this function to something like `uart_stm32_prep_power_transition()`.

However it seems to be more or less generic that the `uart_xx_pm_control` is calling a `uart_xx_set_power_state` function.
The test in the uart_stm32_set_power_state function is just checking that the UART is requested to enter a _non-DEVICE_PM_ACTIVE_STATE_

Only `uart_nrfx_uart.c` is setting the field in device struct outside of `uart_*_set_power_state()`. The other two drivers which have PM enabled, `uart_cc13xx_cc26xx.c` and `uart_nrfx_uarte.c`, are doing this inside the setter function. I still think it is better to actually set the state inside the setter function to be less confusing.
I'm personally still pro at least renaming the function if you want it to keep it separate.
If made public it's worth adding some docstrings
